analysis.title: UBS S&T - European Morning Note - William Day - 2026-11-10
key_insights: VGZ6 (Euro Stoxx 50 futures) +0.9% in early trading after the US rally.

US stocks had their biggest rally in over seven months. The S&P 500 gained 2.3% by the close with all 11 sectors higher, and the Nasdaq closed up 3.4%. UBS calls it the broadest rally in nearly a year.
Crude is at its lowest levels since August (-1% overnight, Brent $91.7, WTI $86.2). The move followed President Trump saying on Monday afternoon that 'Iran, militarily, is effectively over'.
Asia has taken the lead from the US. Chip-heavy benchmarks are off earlier highs but firmly higher: Topix and Taiex +2-3%, KOSPI +5%, and SoftBank about +15% ahead of its earnings release.
Taiwan October exports hit a record, +58.9% YoY against a +51% estimate. Imports and the trade surplus also hit records.

CTA equity exposure has turned negative (-5%). With real money not selling and corporate buybacks returning next week, UBS says the systematic feedback loop that amplifies headline-driven selling has largely been removed.
Cross-asset volatility looks relatively muted ahead of US CPI this afternoon.

On the UBS Equity ETD desk in London, asset managers kept adding to longs across European majors, in excess of $1.5bn. There was buying in Euro Banks and Travel & Leisure. The only sell flow was partial profit taking in OMX.

sector_views.rationale: Desk flow showed buyers of Euro Banks on the UBS Equity ETD desk in London, alongside asset managers adding to longs in European majors.
Desk flow showed buyers of Travel & Leisure on the UBS Equity ETD desk in London. Crude at its lowest since August is the backdrop.

earnings_insights: SoftBank is up about 15% in Tokyo ahead of its earnings release. The note gives no date or estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The note lists 13:30 US CPI MoM Oct 0.3% as the afternoon release. The 0.3% is the expected figure, not a print. Cross-asset volatility is muted ahead of it.
Exports were a record and above the +51% estimate. Imports and the trade surplus were also records, which supports the rally in chip-heavy Asian benchmarks.
Systematic equity exposure has turned negative, which limits further forced selling.

risk_factors: US CPI at 13:30 this afternoon (October MoM, 0.3% expected) is the near-term event risk.
The rally follows a geopolitical headline on Iran, so a reversal in that headline could reverse the move.
Corporate buybacks only return next week, so that support is not yet in place.
